patches.old: The most widely accepted explanation invokes **misapplied size constancy**: the arrowhead configurations serve as depth cues suggesting that one line is the inside corner of a room (farther away) and the other is the outside corner of a building (closer).
patches.new: The most widely accepted explanation invokes **misapplied size constancy**, and it is worth fixing the direction in memory because it is easy to reverse. The fins that **splay outward** from the ends of the shaft read as the **inside corner of a room**, which recedes away from you; since the brain scales a retinal image up with perceived distance, that shaft looks **longer**. The **arrowheads that close back inward** over the shaft read as the **outside corner of a building**, which juts toward you; that shaft looks **shorter**. Same retinal length, two different distance stories, two different percepts.

patches.old: People in carpentered environments learn to associate inward fins with corners receding in depth, making those lines appear longer.
patches.new: People in carpentered environments learn to read outward-splaying fins as the inside corner of a room receding away from them, and because perceived size is scaled by perceived distance, that line looks longer; inward-closing arrowheads read as the near outside corner of a building and look shorter.

sources.title: Illusions Index, University of Edinburgh — the Müller-Lyer illusion, noting the line with outward-pointing arrowheads appears longer and Gregory's distance-scaling account

visual.title: The illusion drawn the right way round
visual.alt: Two Müller-Lyer figures of identical shaft length side by side: the left with fins splaying outward, labelled as reading like an inside corner that is farther away and therefore looking longer, and the right with arrowheads closing inward, reading as a nearer outside corner and looking shorter; a list of the five perceptual constancies; and a list of illusions paired with the mechanism each one exposes.
visual.caption: Outward fins, inside corner, farther, longer. Reverse any one of those four and the whole chain comes out backwards.
